info.title: BizPlay API
info.description: BizPlay platform APIs â chatbot, classifier, and compliance modules.

tags.name: Bots
tags.description: Manage chatbots â each bot has its own purpose, documents, prompts and LLM settings

tags.name: Telegram integration
tags.description: Link a bot to a Telegram bot so external Telegram users can chat with it

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Upload, list, and manage knowledge-base documents. Every document belongs to exactly one bot â only chats with the same bot retrieve from a document's chunks.

tags.name: Kakao integration
tags.description: Link a bot to a KakaoTalk channel via Kakao i Openbuilder Skill webhooks

tags.name: RAG Chat
tags.description: Chat with the RAG-powered assistant and view conversation history

tags.name: Corporations
tags.description: Manage corp rows. corp_no is the natural business code used by bots as a soft reference, and is the API path identifier here. To change a corp's corp_no, delete and re-create.

tags.name: Corp Groups
tags.description: Manage corp_group rows (top of the tenant tree). Each corp belongs to exactly one corp_group.

put.description: PATCH semantics: omitted fields stay unchanged. corp_no is immutable â to change it, delete and re-create. Returns 404 if corpGroupId points at a non-existent group.

delete.description: Removes the corp row. Bots that reference this corp_no keep their soft reference (it's intentional that dangling soft refs are tolerated).

get.summary: Get a corp group by id

put.description: PATCH semantics: omitted fields stay unchanged. Returns 409 if a new corp_group_cd collides with an existing row.

delete.description: Returns 409 if any corp row still references the group â clear or move those corps first.

get.description: Returns every field plus the bot's recommended questions.

put.description: PATCH semantics: omitted fields are left unchanged. When recommendedQuestions is provided (even as an empty list) the entire collection is replaced atomically; pass null to leave existing questions untouched.

delete.description: Removes the bot, its documents (incl. vector chunks and uploaded files), recommended questions, and all chat sessions/messages. Irreversible.

post.summary: Upload a document for a specific bot
post.description: Upload a PDF, DOCX, or TXT file with a title, scoped to one bot. The file is parsed, chunked, embedded with bot_id in chunk metadata, and stored. Only chats with the same bot will retrieve from this document.

parameters.name: botId
parameters.description: Bot UUID this document belongs to

file.description: File to upload (PDF, DOCX, or TXT)

post.summary: Send a chat query to a specific bot
post.description: Submit a question to one bot. The bot's documents are the only chunks considered (vector search is filtered by bot_id), and the bot's own LLM model, temperature, max-tokens, history-turns, top-K, system prompt, and source-expose settings are applied â request body cannot override them. Session ID must be blank or omitted to start a new conversation; if supplied, it continues the existing conversation within that session.

get.description: Returns all corps, sorted by corp_no. Optional ?corpGroupId=N filter restricts to a single group.

post.description: Creates a corp with a unique corp_no. Returns 409 on collision, or 404 if corpGroupId does not exist (hard FK).

get.description: Returns all corp groups, sorted by corp_group_cd.

post.description: Creates a new corp_group with a unique corp_group_cd. Returns 409 on collision.

get.description: Returns compact summaries for every bot in the system, regardless of corp_id, including disabled bots (with isDisabled=true). Use GET /chatbot/api/v1/bots/by-corp/{corpId} to filter by a specific corporation.

post.description: Creates a bot. corpNo is the corp's natural business code, a soft reference to a corporation managed by the external login service â any value is accepted (no local existence check). When omitted, corpNo defaults to the configured default tenant (DEFAULT). llmModel must match a name from GET /chatbot/api/v1/rag/chat/models. llmTemperature is 0.0â1.0 (default 0); historyTurns and topK default to 5; maxAnswerLength is the LLM's maxTokens (default 1024). systemPrompt is optional â when omitted, the static default prompt is applied. recommendedQuestions[] can be seeded inline. Newly-created bots start disabled â call PATCH /chatbot/api/v1/bots/{id}/enable once setup (documents, system prompt, Telegram link, etc.) is complete.

get.summary: Get Telegram integration status for a bot
get.description: Returns whether the bot is linked and the linked Telegram username. Useful for the bot-management UI to show 'Configured â' vs 'Not configured'. Token is never returned.

post.summary: Configure Telegram integration for a bot
post.description: Validates the supplied bot token via Telegram's getMe and starts a background long-polling thread that pulls updates from Telegram on behalf of this bot. No inbound URL is required â the integration works behind any firewall as long as outbound HTTPS to api.telegram.org is allowed. Any prior webhook on the token is dropped, and Telegram's backlog of queued updates is discarded so the first poll cycle returns only fresh messages. The token is stored on the bot row but never returned in any response â only the bot's Telegram-side username is echoed back. Returns 400 if the token is invalid, 404 if the bot doesn't exist, 409 if the token is already linked to another bot in this system.

delete.summary: Remove Telegram integration from a bot
delete.description: Stops the bot's polling thread, drops any residual webhook on Telegram's side (best-effort â local cleanup proceeds even if Telegram is unreachable), and clears the token, username, and offset from the bot row. The bot itself remains; this only severs the Telegram link. Existing telegram_chats mappings will become orphaned but harmless â they'll be recreated if Telegram is re-configured.

get.description: Convenience endpoint for chat UIs that only need the canned starter prompts.

post.summary: Add a recommended question to a bot
post.description: Append a single canned starter prompt to the bot's list. The new question is ordered last (creation-time order). Returns the persisted question with its server-assigned ID.

get.summary: Get Kakao integration status for a bot
get.description: Returns whether the bot is linked, the operator-supplied display name, and the current webhook URL (when the public-base-url is configured). The URL contains the per-bot secret â treat the whole response as sensitive.

post.summary: Configure Kakao integration for a bot
post.description: Generates a fresh per-bot webhook secret and returns the full webhook URL operators paste into Kakao i Openbuilder's Skill configuration. The secret is part of the URL path; the URL as a whole is sensitive and must not be shared outside the operator + Openbuilder. Re-calling this endpoint rotates the secret â the old URL stops working immediately.

delete.summary: Remove Kakao integration from a bot
delete.description: Clears the webhook secret, display name, and configured-at timestamp. After this, the previously-distributed webhook URL returns 404. Existing kakao_chats mappings become orphaned but harmless â they'll be recreated if Kakao is re-configured.

post.summary: Generate a system prompt from a bot's name and description
post.description: Stateless utility â does NOT create a bot. Calls the configured (or supplied) LLM with a meta-prompt that produces a tailored system prompt following the project's three-step source priority (context â history â refuse). Use this as a 'Generate' button on a bot-creation form; the returned text can be edited before being sent to POST /chatbot/api/v1/bots in the systemPrompt field. Falls back to the static default prompt if the LLM call fails or returns blank.

patch.description: Bot is preserved but new chat calls return 409. Documents and history remain.

get.description: Returns metadata for every document uploaded to the given bot.
Retrieve metadata (incl. owning botId) for a single document.

delete.description: Remove a document, the file on disk under uploads/{docId}/, and every vector chunk whose metadata.doc_id matches. Other documents on the same bot are unaffected â to remove all documents of a bot in one shot, delete the bot itself via DELETE /chatbot/api/v1/bots/{id} which cascades.

get.description: View the original uploaded file inline or download it

Returns the list of configured LLM models with a 'default' flag. Use the 'name' value when creating or updating a bot (the 'llmModel' field on BotCreateRequest / BotUpdateRequest). Chat itself does not take a model â each bot stores its own choice.
Retrieve all messages in a chat session. The session is bot-scoped â callers can read any session by ID, but the messages it returns are only the ones from that bot's conversation.

get.summary: Get aggregate statistics for a bot
get.description: Returns counters covering ingested documents (total + per embedding status), chat sessions, persisted messages, conversation turns (user-side messages), recommended questions, and the timestamp of the most recent chat activity. Pass `?windowDays=7` (or 30, 90, etc.) to additionally receive `windowConversationCount`, `windowMessageCount`, and the same metrics for the previous comparable window â useful for the analytics dashboard's KPI cards with their "Up X% compared to the previous period" deltas. Without `windowDays`, only lifetime totals are returned.

parameters.name: windowDays
parameters.description: Optional window size in days (e.g. 7, 30, 90). When provided, the response includes per-window counts and previous-window counts.

get.summary: Popular keywords for a bot's analytics dashboard
get.description: Returns the top-`limit` most frequent keywords across user messages whose `createdAt` falls in [now â windowDays, now). Sorted by count desc, then alphabetically for tie-breaking. Tokens with frequency < 2 are dropped â a single mention is noise, not a "popular" keyword. v1 produces single-word keywords only; multi-word phrases (e.g. "Business trip request") need an LLM topic-extraction pass which is on the roadmap. Returns 404 if the bot does not exist; 400 if windowDays â¤ 0 or limit not in [1, 100].

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many keywords to return (1-100). Defaults to 10.

get.summary: Daily activity series for a bot's analytics dashboard
get.description: Returns one bucket per calendar day inside the requested window (zero-filled â days with no activity still appear with `conversationCount: 0`, `messageCount: 0`). Drives the "Daily conversation count" bar chart. The window is [now â windowDays, now). Returns 404 if the bot does not exist; 400 if windowDays is missing or non-positive.

get.summary: List all chat sessions for a bot
get.description: Returns every chat session belonging to the given bot, ordered newest first. Each entry carries the session ID, when it was created, the timestamp of the most recent message, and total message count (user + assistant). To inspect a single session's full transcript, follow up with GET /chatbot/api/v1/rag/chat/history/{sessionId}. Returns 404 if the bot does not exist; an empty array (200) if the bot exists but has no sessions yet.

get.summary: List bots for a specific corporation
get.description: Returns compact summaries for every bot referencing the given corp_no (including disabled bots). Use this when an admin / cross-tenant view needs to filter the full bot list by a single corporation rather than calling GET /chatbot/api/v1/bots and filtering client-side. corp_no is a soft reference to data owned by the external login service, so unknown codes return an empty list rather than 404.

delete.description: Remove a single recommended question. The question must belong to the bot in the path; otherwise 404 is returned.

corpGroupId.description: Replacement corp_group id. Pass null to leave unchanged.

corpName.description: Replacement display name. Pass null to leave unchanged.

corpGroupCd.description: Replacement natural business code. Pass null to leave unchanged.

recommendedQuestions.description: When provided, replaces the bot's existing recommended questions. Pass an empty list to clear them. Pass null (or omit) to leave them unchanged.

question.description: The canned question text shown to end users
question.example: When can I claim travel expenses?

botId.description: Bot to ask. Required. Must belong to the caller's corporation. Disabled bots reject chat with HTTP 409.

query.example: What is the company leave policy?

sessionId.description: Chat session identifier. â¢ Omit on the FIRST message of a conversation â the server creates a new session bound to the bot in this request and returns its ID in the response (`data.sessionId`). â¢ Pass that ID back on every subsequent message in the same conversation so the server can load prior turns and use them as conversation history (the bot's `historyTurns` setting controls how many turns are included). Sessions enable referential follow-ups like "explain point 2" or "translate that to Korean" â without a sessionId the model has no memory of the previous turn. â¢ A session is owned by exactly one bot. Reusing a session ID with a different `botId` returns HTTP 400. To start a new conversation, omit the field again. â¢ Persisted: see GET /chatbot/api/v1/rag/chat/history/{sessionId} for retrieval.

channel.description: **Optional.** Channel the conversation originates from. Free-form, but the analytics dashboard buckets values into Web / Telegram / KakaoTalk / Others, so prefer one of those values when applicable. Persisted on the session row at creation time and ignored on subsequent messages of the same session. Defaults to "web" when omitted, null, or blank.

corpNo.description: Natural business identifier â issued by the external login service. UNIQUE.

corpGroupId.description: ID of the owning corp_group. Hard FK â must already exist.

corpGroupCd.description: Natural business code for the group (UNIQUE).

corpNo.description: Owning corporation, identified by its natural business code (corp_no). Soft reference to a corp managed by the external login service â any value is accepted, no local existence check. Defaults to the configured default tenant (corp_no=DEFAULT in dev) if omitted.

description.description: Free-form description of what this bot is for

systemPrompt.description: System prompt that frames every chat with this bot. If omitted, a sensible default is used (see BotDefaults).

sourceExpose.description: Whether sources are returned to clients. Defaults to true.

llmModel.description: LLM registry name (see GET /chatbot/api/v1/rag/chat/models for valid values)

maxAnswerLength.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM's reply. Defaults to 1024.

historyTurns.description: How many prior turns of conversation are included in the prompt. Defaults to 5.

topK.description: Number of chunks retrieved per chat. Defaults to 5.

recommendedQuestions.description: Optional pre-canned questions to seed the bot with

token.description: Telegram bot token issued by @BotFather. Format is `<numeric-id>:<35-char-string>`. Stored verbatim and used to authenticate every outbound call to Telegram on behalf of this bot.

botName.description: Optional display label for the linked Kakao i Openbuilder bot, e.g. "ì¶ì¥ê·ì ë´". Surfaced in the bot editor UI only â Kakao does not provide a canonical name in its webhook payloads, so the operator picks something memorable.

name.description: Bot name â used to anchor the prompt's subject

description.description: Free-form description of what the bot is for. The richer the description, the more tailored the generated prompt.
description.example: Helps employees understand and apply the company's domestic and international travel expense reimbursement policy.

llmModel.description: Optional LLM registry name to use for generation. Defaults to the configured default model when omitted.

BotStatistics.description: Aggregate counters describing how much content and chat traffic a bot has accumulated.

botId.description: Bot ID the statistics belong to.

botName.description: Bot name (denormalised here so callers don't need a second GET /bots/{id} call).

documentCount.description: Total documents owned by this bot, regardless of embedding status.

completedDocumentCount.description: Documents whose embedding pipeline has completed successfully.

failedDocumentCount.description: Documents whose embedding pipeline failed â usually require re-upload.

chatSessionCount.description: Number of distinct chat sessions ever opened against this bot.

messageCount.description: Total chat messages persisted for this bot (user + assistant combined).

conversationTurnCount.description: Conversation turns â one user prompt + its assistant reply counts as a single turn, so this equals the number of user-role messages.

recommendedQuestionCount.description: Number of recommended starter questions configured on the bot.

lastChatAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent chat message (user or assistant). Null if the bot has never been chatted with.

windowDays.description: Echo of the requested window size in days (7 / 30 / 90 â¦). Null when the caller did not ask for a windowed breakdown.

windowStart.description: Inclusive lower bound of the requested window. Null if no window requested.

windowEnd.description: Exclusive upper bound of the requested window (â now at request time). Null if no window requested.

windowConversationCount.description: Sessions started inside the window. Null if no window requested.

previousWindowConversationCount.description: Sessions started inside the *previous* comparable window â i.e. [windowStart - windowDays, windowStart). Lets the UI compute the "Up X% compared to the previous period" delta. Null if no window requested.

windowMessageCount.description: Messages persisted inside the window. Null if no window requested.

previousWindowMessageCount.description: Messages persisted inside the previous comparable window. Null if no window requested.

windowTokenUsage.description: Sum of input + output tokens recorded on assistant messages inside the window. Drives the dashboard's "Token usage" KPI. Zero for windows where the LLM did not return a usage block. Null if no window requested.

previousWindowTokenUsage.description: Same metric for the previous comparable window â lets the UI compute the "Up X% compared to the previous period" delta on the token-usage card. Null if no window requested.

channelDistribution.description: Session counts grouped by channel inside the window â drives the "Channel distribution" pie chart. Keys are channel codes as written by clients (e.g. "web", "telegram", "kakaotalk"); values are session counts. Empty map for windows with no activity. Null if no window requested.

languageDistribution.description: User-message counts grouped by detected language inside the window â drives the "Distribution of languages used" widget. Keys are BCP-47-ish two-letter codes (e.g. "ko", "en"); values are message counts. Restricted to user messages so the assistant's echoed language doesn't double-count. Null if no window requested.

KeywordStat.description: A keyword + how many times it appeared across user messages in the window.

count.description: Number of user messages in the window that contained this keyword.

DailyStat.description: One day's bucket of activity for a bot.

date.description: The day this bucket covers (server timezone). Use as the x-axis label.

conversationCount.description: Sessions whose createdAt falls within this calendar day.

ChatSessionSummary.description: Compact summary of a single chat session belonging to a bot.

sessionId.description: Session ID. Use it with GET /chatbot/api/v1/rag/chat/history/{sessionId} to fetch the full transcript.
